drivers.label: Digital input
drivers.description: A contact, button, float switch or PIR read as on/off.
wiring: With pull up (the default), wire the contact between the pin and GND: closed reads 0, open reads 1. Turn on Invert to flip that.
GPIOs 34-39 on the ESP32 have no internal pull resistor: set pull to none and fit a 10 kΩ resistor.

drivers.label: Analog input
drivers.description: A 0-3.3 V sensor. Value = volts × scale + offset.
wiring: Never more than 3.3 V on the pin. For a 0-5 V or 0-10 V sensor, use a voltage divider and fold its ratio into the scale.
Only ADC1 pins read while Wi-Fi is on; the pin picker offers only those.

drivers.label: DS18B20 temperature
drivers.description: 1-Wire temperature probes, up to 4 on one pin.
wiring: Fit a 4.7 kΩ resistor between the data line and 3.3 V (many probe modules already have one).
Power the probes from 3.3 V with 3 wires; parasite power (2 wires) isn't supported.
Several probes share one pin; they're numbered in address order, so swapping a probe can change which is Probe 1.

drivers.label: DHT22 / AM2302
drivers.description: Temperature and humidity on one data pin.
wiring: Power it from 3.3 V. A bare sensor needs a 10 kΩ pull-up from data to 3.3 V; modules usually have one.
It can't be read more often than every 2 seconds.

drivers.label: Pulse counter
drivers.description: Counts pulses: flow meters, anemometers, energy meter pulse outputs, rain gauges.
wiring: Pulses per unit converts pulses to your unit, e.g. 450 for a YF-S201 flow meter in litres.
Open-collector sensors (most flow meters, hall sensors) need the pull-up on.
A 5 V sensor output needs a voltage divider to 3.3 V. Counts up to about 10 kHz.
For a mechanical switch (reed, rain gauge), set Ignore pulses closer than to ~5000 µs to skip bounce.

drivers.label: HC-SR04 distance
drivers.description: Ultrasonic distance, 2-400 cm. Also tank level, measured from the top.
wiring: The HC-SR04 runs on 5 V and its ECHO pin outputs 5 V: put a divider (1 kΩ from ECHO, 2 kΩ to GND) between ECHO and the GPIO, or use the 3.3 V HC-SR04P.
TRIG can be driven straight from the GPIO.
No echo, or anything past Max distance, reads as unknown, not 0.

drivers.label: MPU6050 / GY-521 motion
drivers.description: Accelerometer and gyroscope: tilt, vibration and raw motion.
wiring: Connect VCC to 3.3 V, GND to GND, SDA and SCL to the board's I2C pins (set in the I2C bus row). The GY-521 has its own pull-ups.
AD0 to GND (or unconnected) is address 0x68; AD0 to 3.3 V is 0x69. Two on one bus need different addresses.
Tilt is only meaningful while the board is still. For raw axes, use a metric that publishes as a stream.

drivers.label: Relay / on-off output
drivers.description: A relay module or any output switched on and off.
wiring: Many relay modules switch on when their input is LOW: turn on Active low for those.
Power the relay coil from the module's own VCC (5 V), not from a GPIO.
The output holds its boot state until the platform's desired state arrives.

drivers.label: PWM output
drivers.description: A variable output: dimmers, fan speed, MOSFET modules, buzzers, PWM-to-0-10 V modules.
wiring: Drive loads through a MOSFET or driver module, never straight from the pin.
LED dimming: 1-5 kHz. Fans: 25 kHz. A passive buzzer: its tone's frequency.
Very high frequencies need fewer resolution bits (e.g. 40 kHz at 10 bits).

drivers.label: Servo
drivers.description: A hobby servo (SG90, MG996R...): the command is an angle.
wiring: Power the servo from its own 5 V supply, not the board's 3.3 V, and join the grounds.
If it buzzes or hits the end stops, narrow the pulse widths (e.g. 1000-2000 µs).
